chunk_findings.detail: The fix does not drop GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, or GIT_PREFIX before spawning pytest. It only skips the after-merge path when `_linked_worktree(repo)` reports a linked worktree. Given the regression input the intent calls for — GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE set to a scratch repository — `_linked_worktree` runs `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` and `--git-common-dir` under that GIT_DIR, so both outputs resolve to the scratch repo’s `.git` and the function returns False. Execution then falls through to `PM.after_merge(repo, cfg)`, which spawns pytest as a child still inheriting GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE; the fixtures’ `git init` corrupts the scratch repo exactly as in B683c75d7b3. The same leak remains on the non-after-merge path ending in `_regenerate_outcome` (line 63), so a direct `ddflow pins regenerate` in a linked worktree is also unprotected. The guard must sanitize the subprocess environment (or inspect the leaked GIT_DIR itself), not merely rely on git currently reporting a linked worktree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:50

chunk_findings.detail: The added regression test deletes GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_COMMON_DIR and monkeypatches `PM.after_merge` to a no-op. It therefore never spawns the pytest process whose inherited environment corrupted the worktree, and it cannot detect the leak the bug describes. It would pass even if the production code still spawned pytest with the leaked GIT_* variables on any path other than the guarded after_merge call. The regression test required by the intent — set GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE to a scratch repo and assert that repo remains untouched — is not present.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_pins_hook_git_env.py:19

chunk_findings.detail: The intent's explicit requirement is that the hook drop `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_PREFIX` before spawning any child. The change does not drop any of them; it only substitutes one heuristic. Concretely, on the exact regression input the intent prescribes — a regenerate run whose cwd is a linked worktree but whose environment carries `GIT_DIR=<scratch>/.git` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<scratch>/.git/index` — `_linked_worktree` runs `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` and `--git-common-dir` *under that GIT_DIR*, so both resolve to `<scratch>/.git`, compare equal, and the function returns `False`. The guard therefore does not fire, `PM.after_merge` runs, and its `pytest`/recipe children still inherit `GIT_DIR=<scratch>/.git`. A fixture doing `git init` / `git commit` then re-initializes and commits into `<scratch>`, i.e. the scratch repo the intent's regression test asserts must be untouched is corrupted — the same class of bug (inherited GIT_* redirected into a foreign repo) the change claims to close. The previous HIGH finding on this line still holds: the new guard only covers the case where git itself set `GIT_DIR` to the worktree's private gitdir; it is a false negative whenever `GIT_DIR` points at a common/foreign `.git`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:50 / `_linked_worktree` (ddflow/api/pin_files.py:66)

chunk_findings.detail: The added tests still do not exercise the leaking path. `test_after_merge_hook_skips_a_linked_worktree` removes `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR` and replaces `PM.after_merge` with a stub, so no child process is ever spawned with the hook's environment; it cannot detect any leak on the un-stubbed after-merge path. `test_recipe_child_with_hook_git_env_leaves_the_scratch_repo_untouched` calls `PINS._run` directly, but this diff does not modify `ddflow/services/pins.py` at all, so that test's outcome is byte-for-byte identical before and after the fix: it cannot fail on the unfixed code and therefore is not a regression test for B683c75d7b3. (It also bypasses `PM.after_merge`, the path the intent says spawned the rogue `pytest`.) The regression test the intent asks for — "run the hook's regenerate with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` set to a scratch repo and assert that repo is untouched" — is not present: `test_after_merge_hook_skips_a_linked_worktree` deletes those variables rather than pointing them at a scratch repo.

chunk_findings.detail: The intent states that pins regenerate "*(and any hook-run child)* must drop `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_PREFIX` before spawning pytest". The diff deletes/unsets no environment variable at all; it only adds a single path heuristic that skips `after_merge` when the *repo* path happens to be a linked worktree. Take the intent's own prescribed regression input: run the hook's regenerate from the primary checkout (or any checkout whose `.git` is a directory) with `GIT_DIR=<scratch>/.git` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<scratch>/.git/index`. `_linked_worktree(repo)` returns False because `<primary>/.git` is a directory, control falls through to `PM.after_merge(repo, cfg)`, which spawns `pytest tests/golden --snapshot-update`; those children still inherit the leaked `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`, so the fixture `git init`/`add README.md`/`commit init` act on `<scratch>` — precisely the corruption the bug describes. The added test `test_recipe_child_with_hook_git_env_leaves_the_scratch_repo_untouched` constructs exactly that polluted environment but invokes `PINS._run` (a function this diff does not touch) in a plain non-repo directory, so it never reaches this guard nor the after-merge spawn, and it cannot detect the leak on the path being changed. The earlier HIGH finding therefore still holds: the rewrite of `_linked_worktree` to a path-only check answers the "`git rev-parse` under a stray `GIT_DIR`" mechanism but not the requirement to drop the variables.

chunk_findings.detail: Neither added test exercises the leaking code path. `test_after_merge_hook_skips_a_linked_worktree` deletes `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR` and then monkeypatches `PM.after_merge` to a lambda, so no child process is ever spawned with the hook's environment; it asserts only that the stub was not called, which is a test of the new guard, not of the env leak it is named for. `test_recipe_child_with_hook_git_env_leaves_the_scratch_repo_untouched` calls `PINS._run` directly, and `ddflow/services/pins.py` is not modified by this diff, so that test produces the identical result on the unfixed code — it cannot be "watched to FAIL on the unfixed code" as the intent requires, and if `_run` does not already sanitize the environment this change ships a failing test rather than a fix. The earlier MEDIUM finding is unanswered by this diff.

chunk_findings.detail: `(repo / ".git").is_file()` is true for any checkout whose `.git` is a gitfile, which is not the same set as "linked worktree". A repository created with `git init --separate-git-dir=/elsewhere` (or `git clone --separate-git-dir`, or a submodule checkout) has `work/.git` containing `gitdir: /elsewhere`; in such a checkout `_linked_worktree` returns True, so after `git merge main` the post-merge hook now returns `O.ok("pins", note="pins: post-merge hook skipped in a linked worktree")` and pin regeneration is silently and permanently skipped even though this is the primary/dev checkout, leaving pins stale with no error. The check needs to distinguish a genuine `git worktree add` link (e.g. via the `gitdir` target containing `/worktrees/`, or `rev-parse --git-common-dir` vs `--git-dir`) rather than "is a file".

chunk_findings.detail: The change implements only half of what the bug demands. B683c75d7b3 wants the git environment dropped before any recipe/pytest child is spawned: "pins regenerate (and any hook-run child) must drop GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_PREFIX before spawning pytest". The diff adds only the linked-worktree short-circuit (`if _linked_worktree(repo): return O.ok(...)`) and touches no code that spawns children — `ddflow/services/pins.py` `_run` is unchanged. The accompanying test proves the gap: `test_recipe_child_with_hook_git_env_leaves_the_scratch_repo_untouched` sets `GIT_DIR=<scratch>/.git` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<scratch>/.git/index`, runs `PINS._run(work, r.regen, r, 60, write=True)`, and asserts scratch's reflog is unchanged. With the hook env still inherited, the child `git init` reinitializes `scratch/.git` and `git commit --allow-empty -m init` writes a fresh commit there, so `reflog` gains a `commit (initial): init` entry and the assertion fails — the regression test is red on this change. The same unused path is the real hazard: git sets GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE for every hook, so when the post-merge hook fires in the primary checkout (`_linked_worktree(primary)` is False because its `.git` is a directory), `PM.after_merge` still runs its recipes/pytest with the leaked index and can clobber the primary exactly as described. Only the narrow worktree path is protected; the environment-sanitizing fix that the intent and the new test call for is absent.

chunk_findings.detail: The heuristic resolves *every* conflict hunk in the file whose two sides differ only in runs of digits, not just hunks inside ddflow-managed knob/count regions. `_DIGITS.sub("#", ours) == _DIGITS.sub("#", theirs)` is true for any numeric edit that does not also change surrounding letters, so the hunk is replaced by our side and the merge is reported clean. Concrete input: a pins file whose body contains `timeout: 3`, branch A (ours) changes it to `timeout: 5` and branch B (main, theirs) changes it to `timeout: 9`. `git merge-file` emits one conflict hunk `timeout: 5` / `timeout: 9`; `_DIGITS` maps both to `timeout: #`, `same` is True, `_counts_only` returns `timeout: 5`, and after the recomputed `code = text.count("<<<<<<< ours\n")` is 0 the function returns the merged text with `conflicted=False`. Main's edit is dropped with no conflict marker and no warning, and `ddflow pins regenerate` (which only re-records generated regions, not arbitrary prose/config values) has nothing to recover from — the exact silent-data-loss class the caller can no longer detect. The same happens for a date line (`Released 2024-01-05` vs `2025-02-06`) or a version (`v1.2.3` vs `v1.2.4`), both common in READMEs: all digits become `#` and the two sides compare equal. Before this change those inputs surfaced as conflicts; now they are silently resolved toward ours while the caller is told the merge is clean.
